info.title: TeachMeHIPAA Developer API
info.description:
The TeachMeHIPAA API is organized around REST. It has predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON request bodies (form-encoded for access tokens, CSV for imports), returns JSON responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication and verbs.

You can use the API in the Sandbox, which doesn't email real learners. The Sandbox and live have separate servers and separate API clients.

The API covers the training lifecycle of an organization: add learners, invite them to a course, follow their progress, and collect their certificates. Subscribe to webhooks to hear about changes instead of polling.

## Authentication

The API uses OAuth 2.0 access tokens. An organization admin creates an API client in the TeachMeHIPAA console; the client secret is shown once, so store it securely and never in client-side code.

Exchange the client id and secret for an access token at `POST /v1/auth/token` with `grant_type=client_credentials`, authenticating with HTTP Basic. Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every other request. Tokens last 15 minutes and there is no refresh token: request a new one when it expires. `GET /v1/auth/introspection` tells you what a token holds.

Requests without a valid token fail with `401`, and requests whose token lacks the scope an operation needs fail with `403`.

## Errors

TeachMeHIPAA uses conventional HTTP response codes. Codes in the `2xx` range mean success, codes in the `4xx` range mean the request can't be fulfilled as sent (a missing parameter, a conflict with the resource's state), and codes in the `5xx` range mean something went wrong on our side.

Errors are returned as Problem Details (`application/problem+json`, RFC 9457). Every error has a `status`, a short `title`, and a machine-readable `code` you can branch on, such as `seat_unavailable` or `illegal_transition`; `detail` explains this occurrence, and `errors` lists each invalid field with its `path` and `message`. The token endpoint is the exception: it answers in the OAuth 2.0 shape, `{ error, error_description }`.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `200` `201` `202` `204` | Success. `202` means accepted for processing. |
| `304` | Not modified: your cached copy is current. |
| `400` | Bad request: the request couldn't be read. |
| `401` | Unauthorized: no valid access token. |
| `403` | Forbidden: the token lacks the required scope or limit. |
| `404` | Not found, including a resource in another organization. |
| `409` | Conflict with the resource's current state. |
| `412` `428` | A required `If-Match` is stale or missing. |
| `415` | Unsupported content type. |
| `422` | Validation failed; see `errors`. |
| `429` | Too many requests; wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `502` `503` | Something went wrong on our side; retry later. |

## Pagination

List operations return a page of results with `items` and `nextCursor`. Pass `limit` to set the page size and the previous page's `nextCursor` as `cursor` to get the next page. When `nextCursor` is `null`, you've reached the end. Cursors are opaque: don't build or edit them. List responses also carry a `Link` header with `rel="next"` (RFC 8288).

Some filters are applied per page, so a page can hold fewer than `limit` items while `nextCursor` still points to more. Keep paging until `nextCursor` is `null`.

## Idempotent requests

Operations that create or change something require an `Idempotency-Key` header, so you can retry them safely after a network error without doing the work twice. Use a unique value per operation, such as a UUID.

For 24 hours, a retry with the same key and body returns the first response without running the operation again. Reusing a key with a different body fails with `422` `idempotency_key_reuse`.

## Conditional requests

Resources carry a strong `ETag`. Send it back as `If-None-Match` on a `GET` to get `304 Not Modified` when nothing changed. Updates that require `If-Match` fail with `428` when it's missing and `412` when the resource changed since you read it: read it again and retry.

## Sandbox

Build against the **Sandbox (test mode)** server before you go live. Create Sandbox API clients in the staging console and use them only with the Sandbox server: a test-mode client can't get a token from the live server, and a live client can't get one from the Sandbox.

The Sandbox only emails addresses on the staging allowlist.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description:
Access tokens authenticate every other request. Get one with your client credentials and send it as a bearer token. Tokens last 15 minutes.

### The access token object

#### Attributes

- **`access_token`** *string*  
  The access token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer`.
- **`token_type`** *enum*  
  Always `Bearer`.
- **`expires_in`** *integer*  
  Seconds until the token expires.
- **`scope`** *string*  
  The scopes the token holds, space-delimited.

tags.name: Courses
tags.description:
Courses are the trainings TeachMeHIPAA offers. The catalog is public: you can list and retrieve courses without an access token.

### The Course object

#### Attributes

- **`courseId`** *string*  
  Unique identifier for the course.
- **`title`** *string*  
  The course's title.
- **`courseVersion`** *string*  
  The current version of the course content.
- **`passingThreshold`** *number*  
  The score needed to pass the course's assessment.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description:
An organization is the account your API client belongs to. Every invite uses one seat, so check the seat inventory before inviting learners in bulk.

### The Seat inventory object

#### Attributes

- **`purchased`** *integer*  
  Seats the organization holds and hasn't been refunded for, including a trial seat.
- **`assigned`** *integer*  
  Seats held by an invited or enrolled learner.
- **`available`** *integer*  
  Seats a new invite can use now.

<details><summary>More attributes</summary>

- **`total`** *integer*  
  All seats on record.
- **`used`** *integer*  
  Seats in use.
- **`byState`** *object*  
  Seats by internal state. Prefer `purchased`, `assigned` and `available`.

</details>

tags.name: Members
tags.description:
Members are the people in an organization: its admins and its learners. A member is addressed by `subjectId`, which is also the learner's `learnerId`.

### The Member object

#### Attributes

- **`subjectId`** *nullable string*  
  Unique identifier for the member. `null` for an older member who can't be addressed yet.
- **`email`** *string*  
  The member's email address.
- **`name`** *nullable string*  
  The member's full name.
- **`role`** *enum*  
  `admin` or `learner`.
- **`isDisabled`** *boolean*  
  Whether the member's account is disabled.

tags.name: Learners
tags.description:
A learner is a person your organization trains in one course. The learner object combines their membership, enrollment and current certificate, so one call tells you where they stand: invited, in progress, compliant, expiring soon or expired. Use learners for most integrations; use enrollments when you need the underlying lifecycle.

### The Learner object

#### Attributes

- **`learnerId`** *string*  
  Unique identifier for the learner. The same as the member's `subjectId`.
- **`email`** *string*  
  The learner's email address.
- **`name`** *nullable string*  
  The learner's full name.
- **`externalId`** *nullable string*  
  Your own id for the learner, unique within the organization.
- **`status`** *enum*  
  The learner's training status in this course. One of `not_started` (invited), `invite_bounced`, `in_progress`, `compliant`, `expiring_soon` (within 60 days of expiry), `expired` or `removed`.
- **`course`** *object*  
  The course this learner record is for.
- **`certificate`** *nullable object*  
  The learner's current certificate, with its verification and PDF links.

<details><summary>More attributes</summary>

- **`invitedAt`** *nullable string*  
  When the learner was invited (ISO 8601).
- **`startedAt`** *nullable string*  
  When the learner started training.
- **`completedAt`** *nullable string*  
  When the learner completed the course.
- **`dueAt`** *nullable string*  
  When the learner's training is due.

</details>

tags.name: Compliance
tags.description:
The compliance summary counts an organization's learners in one course by status, using the same statuses as the learner object. Use it for dashboards; list learners with a `status` filter for the people behind each count.

### The Compliance summary object

#### Attributes

- **`courseId`** *string*  
  The course.
- **`asOf`** *string*  
  When the counts were taken (ISO 8601).
- **`totals`** *object*  
  Learners by status: `learners`, `compliant`, `expiringSoon`, `expired`, `inProgress`, `notStarted` and `inviteBounced`.
- **`compliantRate`** *number*  
  `compliant` divided by `learners`, or 0 with no learners.

tags.name: Enrollments
tags.description:
An enrollment is one learner's place in one course for one certification cycle. It moves from invited, to started, to certified, and can be cancelled while it's still an invite. Renewing a certified enrollment opens the next cycle.

### The Enrollment object

#### Attributes

- **`enrollmentId`** *string*  
  Unique identifier for the enrollment.
- **`subjectId`** *string*  
  The learner's member id.
- **`courseId`** *string*  
  The course.
- **`status`** *enum*  
  The stored lifecycle state: `INVITED`, `EMAIL_BOUNCED`, `STARTED`, `ASSESSMENT_IN_PROGRESS`, `CERTIFIED` or `CANCELLED`.
- **`effectiveStatus`** *enum*  
  The status to display. Adds `EXPIRING`, `EXPIRED` and `ARCHIVED`, derived when you read it.
- **`cycle`** *integer*  
  The certification cycle, starting at 0. Renewing adds one.
- **`certificateId`** *nullable string*  
  The certificate issued for this cycle, if any.

<details><summary>More attributes</summary>

- **`orgId`** *string*  
  The organization's id.
- **`archived`** *boolean*  
  Whether the enrollment is archived.
- **`rev`** *integer*  
  The resource's revision. Its strong `ETag` is derived from it.
- **`invitedAt`** *nullable string*  
  When the learner was invited (ISO 8601).
- **`startedAt`** *nullable string*  
  When the learner started.
- **`completedAt`** *nullable string*  
  When the learner completed the course.
- **`certifiedAt`** *nullable string*  
  When the learner was certified.
- **`expiresAt`** *nullable string*  
  When the certification expires.

</details>

tags.name: Certificates
tags.description:
A certificate is issued when a learner passes a course. It carries its issue and expiry dates and whether it's valid, expired or revoked. You can download it as a PDF and get its LinkedIn and shareable verification links.

### The Certificate object

#### Attributes

- **`certificateId`** *string*  
  Unique identifier for the certificate.
- **`subjectId`** *nullable string*  
  The holder's member id.
- **`courseId`** *string*  
  The course the certificate is for.
- **`status`** *enum*  
  `VALID`, `EXPIRED` or `REVOKED`.
- **`issuedAt`** *nullable string*  
  When it was issued (ISO 8601).
- **`expiresAt`** *nullable string*  
  When it expires.

<details><summary>More attributes</summary>

- **`holderStatus`** *enum*  
  Whether the holder could be resolved: `resolved`, `none` or `lookup_failed`.
- **`courseVersion`** *nullable string*  
  The course version the holder passed.
- **`revokedAt`** *nullable string*  
  When it was revoked, if it was.

</details>

tags.name: Certificate Verification
tags.description:
Anyone can verify a certificate from its `tme.so` link, without an access token. Verification shows whether the certificate is valid, who it was issued to, the course and its dates, and never the learner's email or any internal id.

### The Certificate verification object

#### Attributes

- **`status`** *enum*  
  `valid`, `expired` or `revoked`.
- **`learnerName`** *string*  
  The name printed on the certificate.
- **`courseTitle`** *string*  
  The course.
- **`issuedAt`** *string*  
  When it was issued (ISO 8601).
- **`expiresAt`** *string*  
  When it expires.

<details><summary>More attributes</summary>

- **`issuer`** *enum*  
  Who issued it.

</details>

tags.name: Audit Events
tags.description: The audit log is the organization's append-only compliance record. Every change to enrollments, certificates, members, settings and API clients is recorded with who made it and when, newest first. Each event has a `type` and the fields of its family; writes made with an API client's token record that client as the `actor`.

tags.name: Bulk Operations
tags.description:
Bulk operations act on many enrollments at once: send reminders, cancel or renew a selection, invite learners from a CSV file, and export rosters and certificate records. Long-running work answers with an operation you can poll; each item reports its own outcome, so one failure never stops the rest.

### The Operation object

#### Attributes

- **`name`** *string*  
  Unique identifier for the operation.
- **`done`** *boolean*  
  Whether the operation has finished.
- **`response`** *object*  
  The result, once `done` is `true`.
- **`error`** *object*  
  The problem, if the operation failed.

<details><summary>More attributes</summary>

- **`metadata`** *object*  
  Progress information, if any.

</details>

tags.name: Webhook Subscriptions
tags.description:
Webhook subscriptions deliver signed events to your HTTPS endpoint as they happen, so you don't have to poll. Each subscription has its own signing secret, shown once when you create it.

### The Webhook subscription object

#### Attributes

- **`subscriptionId`** *string*  
  Unique identifier for the subscription.
- **`endpointUrl`** *string*  
  The HTTPS URL events are delivered to.
- **`eventTypes`** *array of strings*  
  The event types delivered.
- **`enabled`** *boolean*  
  Whether deliveries are on.
- **`secretKeyId`** *string*  
  Identifies the signing secret. Sent as `x-tmh-key-id`.

<details><summary>More attributes</summary>

- **`description`** *nullable string*  
  Your description of the subscription.
- **`seatsLowThreshold`** *integer*  
  Send `seats.low` when available seats drop to this number. Defaults to 5.
- **`createdAt`** *string*  
  When it was created (ISO 8601).
- **`rev`** *integer*  
  The resource's revision. Its strong `ETag` is derived from it.

</details>

### Verifying a delivery

Each delivery is a `POST` with these headers: `x-tmh-key-id` (the subscription's `secretKeyId`), `x-tmh-timestamp`, `x-tmh-body-hash` (hex SHA-256 of the raw body), `x-tmh-signature`, `x-tmh-event-type` and `x-tmh-event-id`.

The signature is the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the subscription's secret, of four lines joined by `\n`: `POST`, your endpoint's path and query, `x-tmh-timestamp`, and the body hash. Recompute it over the raw body, compare in constant time, and reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes from your clock. Deliveries are retried up to 12 times, so deduplicate on `eventId`.

tags.name: Events
tags.description:
Events are the same envelopes webhooks deliver, kept for 30 days. The event log is the source of truth: use it to catch up after a missed delivery or an outage. Every event is logged whether or not a subscription listens for it.

### The Event object

#### Attributes

- **`eventId`** *string*  
  Unique identifier for the event. Ids sort by time.

- **`eventType`** *string*  
  The event's type, such as `learner.certified`.

- **`orgId`** *string*  
  The organization the event happened in.

- **`occurredAt`** *string*  
  When it happened (ISO 8601).

- **`data`** *object*  
  The event's payload. Its shape depends on `eventType`.

#### Event types

| Type | Sent when |
| --- | --- |
| `learner.invited` | A learner is invited, or re-invited for a new cycle. |
| `learner.started` | A learner starts training. |
| `learner.certified` | A learner certifies. |
| `enrollment.certified` | A learner certifies (ids only). |
| `learner.expiring` | A certificate enters its 60-day expiry window. |
| `learner.expired` | A certificate expires. |
| `learner.removed` | An invite is cancelled or a learner is removed. |
| `invite.bounced` | An invite email bounces. |
| `certificate.revoked` | An admin revokes a certificate. |
| `seats.low` | Available seats drop to the subscription's threshold. |

bearerAuth.description: OAuth 2.0. **API clients** (one organization) use client credentials (RFC 6749 §4.4). POST `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` `grant_type=client_credentials` (optionally `scope`, space-delimited) to the token URL, authenticated with your client id and secret as HTTP Basic (or `client_id` and `client_secret` form fields). The response's `access_token` is a JWT valid for 15 minutes (`expires_in`), bound to the client's organization; send it as `Authorization: Bearer`. There is no refresh token: run the grant again when the token expires. A client can only ever hold the scopes listed here. Conforms to JWT best current practices (RFC8725): the signing `alg` is pinned, and `iss`/`aud`/`exp` are validated on every request.

scopes.enrollments:write: Create and transition enrollments and assessment attempts.
scopes.certificates:read: Read certificates and download certificate artifacts.
scopes.members:read: Read organization members and the organization record.
scopes.audit:read: Read the organization's audit-event trail and event log.
scopes.learners:write: API clients: create and update learners.
scopes.compliance:read: API clients: read the compliance summary.
scopes.webhooks:manage: API clients: manage webhook subscriptions and read the event log.

get.description: Returns a list of the courses in the public catalog. Needs no access token.

422.description: Invalid pagination query.

404.description: No such course.

200.description: Returns the organization's seat inventory object.

get.description: Returns a list of the organization's members, its admins and learners. Pass `role=admin` to list only admins.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Opt-in, comma-separated. With `enrollmentSubject`, a member whose `subjectId` is null carries `enrollmentSubjectId`: the subject their email resolves to (a never-signed-in invitee), or null when none. Use it only to match the member to Enrollments; it is not an address for member routes. With `holdsInvitation`, each learner carries `holdsInvitation`: whether the organization has an invitation for their email or a Seat bound to them. Each key is omitted when its lookup failed.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Only admins (paginated).

200.description: A dictionary with an `items` array of members and a `nextCursor`.

Link.description: RFC 8288 pagination: `<url>; rel="next"` when more remain.

403.description: Token lacks `members:read`, or the organization is not the token's active org (`org_not_active`).

404.description: No such organization.

422.description: Invalid pagination, `include` or filter query.

200.description: Returns a member object if a valid identifier was provided.

403.description: Token lacks `members:read`, or the organization is not the token's active org (`org_not_active`).

404.description: No such member in this organization (including a well-formed id belonging to another tenant).

get.description: Retrieves a member of the organization.
Returns a list of the organization's enrollments. Filter by `status`, `courseId` or `archived`. Requires the `enrollments:read` scope.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter on the derived effectiveStatus.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Opt-in enrichment. With `priorCertificate`, an item carries `priorCertificate` (object, or null when the server confirmed there is none). The key is omitted on an item whose answer is unknown, and on every item of the page if the certificate lookup failed; clients must treat a missing key as unknown, never as null.

200.description: A dictionary with an `items` array of enrollments and a `nextCursor`.

Link.description: RFC 8288 pagination: `<url>; rel="next"` when more remain.
